02

Explore the evidence

Read all three comparison guides

Find what is absent

Reply A acknowledges; B confuses fields; C states a practical uncertainty; D restates the card.

What next move responds to each reply?

  • For A, invite an own-words account instead of assuming the whole plan was understood.
  • For B, clarify time and room; for C, address the location question rather than simply reciting the card again.

Do not score intelligence, politeness or compliance from these replies.

Respond and check again

The revised explanation is followed by a scripted restatement.

What claim does that restatement support within this exercise?

  • It matches the authored time and room fields.
  • It does not establish future attendance, treatment understanding or a real person’s comprehension.

The script is not participant evidence.

Separate two language needs

The access branch requests both spoken support and a written reminder.

What remains to be arranged before assuming the exchange is accessible?

  • Recognize the need for appropriate qualified spoken support.
  • Treat the written translation as a separate task; do not call generated wording verified.

This lesson supplies no clinical translation or current legal compliance decision.

One notebook for this exploration revision, up to 1,500 characters. Notes stay in this browser. Shared links contain selections only. Nothing is sent to a server.

03

Try the idea elsewhere

Write a non-shaming response to C and a follow-up question that addresses the actual uncertainty. Then state one outcome that a correct scripted reply still cannot prove.

What a careful explanation includes
  • Distinguish acknowledgement from an account of the plan.
  • Address the specific uncertainty and check again.
  • Keep language support and written translation explicit.
  • Separate scripted correspondence from observed understanding.

There is no automatic score for your written interpretation. Use the guide to inspect your reasoning.

docs/verification/universal-author-seque.text:
# Remaining sequence authoring — 23 October 2026

Ten original local lessons extend the eight pilots to three lessons each. Source evidence binds the unchanged historical sequence register; newly read legal/health pages have separately dated scope. The exercise is narrower wherever a selected object, language, physical event or current legal/clinical claim lacks evidence. Independent review is not required by the current user instruction. Missing observations are not converted to passes.

All quotations are excluded from these ten lessons. Original source summaries, fictional cases, sample values and plan coordinates carry explicit provenance and scope. New native model code is not required: existing source-comparison and annotation controls supply the tasks and full static guides.

The continuation command passed all 29 model/source groups across the five named suites, including exact retained-source comparisons, sample-ratio arithmetic, patch predicates and staging changes. A floating-point equality assertion was corrected to a numerical tolerance; the underlying rational example is unchanged.

The native browser group exercised all ten lessons at 320 px, in both themes, with and without JavaScript: all source passages, static guides and transfer tasks were present; controls and private notes survived reload; no horizontal page overflow, script errors or external requests were observed. The initial harness looked for the transfer task inside the guide rather than its separate transfer section; that selector was corrected. Craft and health static screenshots were visually inspected and readable.

These are author checks on local artifacts. No real-world observation, external reviewer approval or public release is recorded. Logs and screenshots: /tmp/atlas-author-continuation-20261023/sequences-check2.log, sequences-ui2.log and sequences-shots/. The receipt is retained with the frozen editions; later delivery evidence belongs in a subsequent receipt.
